transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

It is unlikely that the motor is failing. The symptoms you describe—louder noise and faster battery drain specifically when moving from hard floors to carpet—are actually normal behaviour for the Dyson V15 Detect. The V15 has an 'Auto' mode that uses a piezo sensor to count dust particles. When it detects more resistance (like a rug) or potentially more dust, it automatically ramps up the motor speed to maintain suction. This higher speed draws more power (hence the battery drop) and sounds louder. The screen fluctuating is likely the laser dust counter reacting to the different texture of the rug fibres. To confirm this is just the machine doing its job:
1. Check if you are in 'Auto' mode (the icon on the LCD should show an 'A').
2. If it is, try switching to 'Eco' or 'Mid' mode and test it on the rug again. Does the noise and battery drop still happen when you manually set it to a lower power level?

I checked, and the screen says 'Auto'. I pressed the mode button once and it went to that; the other options are Eco and Boost. I switched it to Eco and tried the rug again, and it stays the same quiet sound on the rug and the tiles.

That suggests it is working exactly as designed. In 'Auto' mode, the V15 Detect uses a laser and sensor to detect dust density and surface resistance; when you move onto a rug, it ramps up power to maintain suction, which naturally sounds louder and drains the battery faster. The screen fluctuations are part of that same data-reading process. Since switching to Eco (a fixed low speed) removes the noise and battery drop, there is no fault with the motor or electronics. You do not need to report this as a defect. It is normal behaviour for this model. If you prefer consistent noise levels and battery usage regardless of floor type, simply keep it in 'Eco' or 'Mid' mode when moving between surfaces.

candidates: Auto mode adjusting suction for carpet depth (high)
Laser dust detection reacting to rug texture/fibres (medium)
